card.name: Chronic dosing in long-term studies
card.fires_on: The word "chronic" itself, its ending "ically" in "chronically", or the noun right after it (administration, treatment). It appears when describing long-term drug exposure, mostly in animal studies.

modes.label: Noun after chronic
modes.description: The word administration or treatment right after "chronic" in long-term exposure statements.
modes.example: ucosa Abnormalities Chronic<< administration>> of desmopressin nasal spray

modes.label: Chronic or chronically
modes.description: The word chronic, or the ending of chronically, describing long-term treated animals.
modes.example: cal mass. 5.12 Ovarian Cysts A dose-related increase in incidence of ovarian cysts was observed in female rats treated chron<<ically>> with oral baclofen.

card.plain: It marks wording about long-term, repeated drug exposure, usually in animal toxicology findings.
